Hi Amelia — thanks for the files. Dropped a quick ingested sample into our sizing harness and flagged a few patterns. High level reply below and we'll follow up with a formal PDF.

Quick findings:~
- Effective sequence distribution is bimodal: ~60% short (<=1k tokens), ~40% long (1k–8k). The long tail drives KV cache pressure and per-request memory.
- If you run FP16 baseline (no quant) we estimate ~6x the vRAM per replica compared to a 4-bit quantized variant for the same model family and context.
- Offloading hot KV pages to host memory saves ~15–25% GPU footprint for long-context requests but increases latency outliers on cold misses.

Proposal (short):~
1) Stage 0 (Canary): 2x A100-80GB equivalents, FP16, KV caching enabled with small warm-up cache — validate latency SLOs.
2) Stage 1 (Reserved commit): 6–8x A100-80GB equivalents with mixed precision (FP16) and conservative KV offload policy for predictable tail latency.
3) Stage 2 (Cost-optimized): Replace up to 50% of fleet with 4-bit quantized variants (Q4_* or GPTQ-style) for non-regression workloads (summaries), reduce committed GPU count by ~30% vs Stage 1.

Action items: Marcus and Soojin to run a sensitivity matrix (vRAM vs quant vs KV hit rate) and produce the committed cost delta for finance. Karthik to map the rollout timeline and fallback model routing rules.

We'll attach the PDF proposal and the sensitivity matrix once done. Is a 2-week cadence to decision realistic for you?

Best,
Avery Johnson
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Statera Health — internal sensitivity matrix (draft)

Team — early draft notes from running Statera's traces through the allocator harness. I attached the CSV outputs to the internal doc; summarizing below.

Summary of simulated points (baseline model family = open-LargeX):~
- Config A (FP16, no offload): per-rep vRAM = ~62GB for 8k worst-case sequences, throughput ~35 tok/s, need 10 replicas to hit peak concurrency with 25% headroom.
- Config B (FP16, host KV offload): per-rep vRAM = ~50GB, throughput ~32 tok/s, requires 8 replicas with higher tail latency variability.
- Config C (Q4x4 quantized, aggressive KV eviction): per-rep vRAM = ~28–32GB, throughput drops ~10% on generation, need 6 replicas; some systematic quality delta observed on a small percentage of medical summaries (we flagged ~4% regression on BLEU-like metric).

Tradeoffs and recommended committed pool:~
- For a 12-month reserved contract we recommend committing 8 A100-80GB equiv (Stage 1) with a policy to auto-flip up to 12 during documented batch peaks. This gives predictable latency and keeps a 20–30% utilization buffer.
- After 60 days of production telemetry, move 40–50% of baseline traffic to Q4 variants with canary checks (Stage 2). This should lower committed GPU needs from 8 -> ~6 and reduce monthly committed cost by ~28% (model license and infra delta included).
- Maintain a 2-rep FP16 hot path for critical requests (real-time clinical queries) to avoid quality/regression excursions.

Notes: host KV offload reduces committed GPUs but requires ops to accept increased variance and more aggressive observability hooks (latency percentiles + eviction rate dashboards).

I'll convert these numbers into a 1-page table for procurement.

—Marcus
